_comment: Device readiness rules. DATA, not code: the category engine, day-one checklist, product-code list and all citations are read from here. Cite ONLY the keys in `citations` below; never invent regulations, guidance names, dates or URLs. See .kiro/specs/device-readiness.
disclaimer: Decision support only, not regulatory advice. Confirm with a regulatory professional or ask FDA (513(g) request or Q-Submission).
incomplete_data_notice: Patterns from public FDA reports for similar devices. Reports are incomplete and have no usage denominator, so counts are not failure rates. Use this to decide where to look first, not to predict your device's faults.

general_wellness.label: Likely general wellness (not a device)
general_wellness.headline: This is likely general wellness, not a medical device.

borderline.label: Borderline
borderline.headline: This is likely borderline: it may be general wellness or a device depending on how it is presented and used.

class_i.label: Likely device: Class I
class_i.headline: This is likely a medical device, most likely Class I.

class_ii.label: Likely device: Class II, 510(k) if a predicate exists, otherwise De Novo
class_ii.headline: This is likely a Class II medical device: 510(k) if a cleared predicate exists, otherwise De Novo.

class_iii.label: Likely device: Class III, PMA
class_iii.headline: This is likely a Class III medical device requiring premarket approval (PMA).

driver_text.claim.flag: Flags a possible disease or condition
driver_text.invasive: Invasive, implanted, or delivers energy or a substance into the body
driver_text.disease_claim: Marketing or app names a specific disease or condition
driver_text.worst.none: Worst realistic outcome is no harm
driver_text.worst.serious: Worst realistic outcome is serious injury
driver_text.users.both: Used by both consumers and clinicians
driver_text.predicate.yes: An already-cleared device does the same thing
driver_text.predicate.no: No already-cleared device does the same thing
driver_text.predicate.unsure: It is unclear whether a cleared device does the same thing

class_i_note.name: Check the classification regulation
class_i_note.when: many Class I devices are exempt from 510(k)

borderline_wellness.name: May be general wellness
borderline_wellness.when: presented as wellness information with no disease claim and no diagnostic use (January 2026 General Wellness guidance)

borderline_device.name: Otherwise a device
borderline_device.when: presented or used to address a specific disease or to diagnose

gw_guidance.label: FDA guidance "General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices" (updated January 2026)

cds_guidance.label: FDA guidance "Clinical Decision Support Software" (updated January 2026)

reg_807.label: 21 CFR Part 807 (establishment registration and device listing)

reg_820_qmsr.label: 21 CFR Part 820, the Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR), aligned with ISO 13485

reg_806.label: 21 CFR Part 806 (reports of corrections and removals)

fdc_524b.label: FD&C Act section 524B (cybersecurity for cyber devices)

day_one_checklist.text: Quality management system: QMSR aligned with ISO 13485, in effect since 2 February 2026
Medical Device Reporting: deaths, serious injuries and malfunctions within 30 calendar days, 5 work days when remedial action is needed
Reports of corrections and removals within 10 working days
Cybersecurity requirements for connected cyber devices
Audit trail of who decided what and when
